title: Choose the smallest useful design
summary: Compare designs by clarity and the changes you expect. A function, a plain object or a pattern can each be the right choice.
introduction: Compare designs by clarity and the changes you expect. A function, a plain object or a pattern can each be the right choice. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain choose the smallest useful design
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Compare designs by clarity and the changes you expect. A function, a plain object or a pattern can each be the right choice.

blocks.code:
const discounts = { none: n => n, half: n => n / 2 };
console.log(discounts.half(12));
blocks.title: Choose the smallest useful design

blocks.text: The result is 6. A small strategy table is enough for these two rules.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not force all patterns into one project. Use only the ones that solve a clear need.
For more detail later, use this [Design Patterns further reading](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns).
